angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the radius and distance: 2 x 523,166.4 km at 19.776 pc = 0.354 mas. The measured limb-darkened diameter is 0.3848 mas (Boyajian et al. 2015, MNRAS 447, 846, CHARA in the H band, as the JMDC lists it), 9 percent larger; the sphere keeps the eclipse map's stellar radius so the planet's orbit and size, fitted in units of it, stay as published.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 50.567 +/- 0.016 mas (photometry/gaia-dr3-source.csv): 1000/50.567 = 19.776 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: 0.752 solar radii (523,166.4 km at 695,700 km per solar radius), the stellar radius Lally et al. (2025, arXiv:2503.20895, Table 1) fix for their eclipse map of HD 189733b. A model-dependent value; the interferometric diameter above gives 0.818 solar radii at the Gaia distance.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the map paper's radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json) and dimmed toward the limb by a law fitted to TESS transits, because no image of the photosphere exists (see investigations.json). A star's limb is not a sharp surface.
